overall: Overnight temperatures in Los Angeles have been remarkably flat, holding steady at roughly 66°F with essentially zero velocity and a negligible trend slope of -0.023°F/hr, indicating a persistent marine layer and cloud cover suppressing any early warming. Patchy fog and mostly cloudy skies (consistent with the NWS narrative) are delaying the typical morning warm-up, and the heat advisory doesn't kick in until Sunday — today remains a cooler, marine-influenced day. The running max of 66.9°F reflects that virtually no daytime heating has occurred yet.
forecast_obs_notes: The three deterministic NWP models (GFS 76.8°F, ECMWF 76.6°F, HRRR 75.8°F) cluster notably warmer than both NBM (71.5°F) and the D1_NOW probability model, which assigns 58.4% to the 72–73°F bucket and 43.0% to 74–75°F. NBM, which blends observations and tends to capture boundary-layer suppression better, is a meaningful outlier on the cool side and aligns more closely with the D1_NOW distribution; the raw NWP models may be underweighting the marine layer and fog persistence.
max_temp_prediction: Given the persistent cloud cover, morning fog, and strong marine influence, the most likely outcome is a high in the 73–74°F range, the top ODD bucket at 49.3%. The D1_NOW model heavily favors 72–74°F combined, and NBM's cooler 71.5°F forecast further supports a cap well below the GFS/ECMWF/HRRR consensus of 75–77°F. Confidence is moderate-to-good (Tier 2 per ensemble signals): the marine layer is a reliable suppressor today, but partial afternoon clearing could nudge temps toward 74–75°F if fog clears earlier than 11am.
